content.objectives: Represent relations with ordered pairs, decide whether a relation is a function, and evaluate simple composite functions.
content.reading: A relation pairs inputs with outputs. A function is stricter: every allowed input has exactly one output. Several inputs may share an output, but one input may not split into two outputs.
content.deep_explanation:
ORDER MATTERS
(x,y) identifies input then output; reversing the pair changes the relation.

VERTICAL-LINE IDEA
A graph is a function when no vertical line meets it more than once.

COMPOSITION IS A PIPELINE
For f∘g, g acts first. Its output becomes the input of f.
content.examples:
If g(x)=x+1 and f(x)=2x, then (f∘g)(3)=f(4)=8.

The relation {(1,a),(2,a),(3,b)} is a function because every input appears with exactly one output.
content.practice:
1. Decide whether {(1,2),(1,3),(2,4)} is a function.
2. If f(x)=3x−1, find f(5).
3. If g(x)=x² and f(x)=x+2, find (g∘f)(2) and (f∘g)(2).
4. Explain why a circle fails the vertical-line test.
content.practice_answers:
1. No; input 1 has two outputs.
2. 14.
3. (g∘f)(2)=16; (f∘g)(2)=6.
4. Some vertical lines meet a circle twice, giving one x two y-values.
content.summary: Functions control outputs. Ordered pairs carry direction. Composition order matters.

quiz.question: Which condition must every function satisfy?

options.B: Every input has exactly one output
